signals.signal: Swipe-away rate is now the #1 ranking signal for Shorts distribution, surpassing raw watch time as the primary indicator of whether distribution expands.
signals.raw_quote: The most important metric is the ratio of swipes to views, which now occupies first place among all indicators.

signals.signal: Shorts with 70%+ completion rates receive ~30% more algorithmic promotion; improving retention by 10 percentage points correlates with 25% more impressions.
signals.raw_quote: Over 70% completion rates yield roughly 30% more algorithmic promotion.

signals.signal: 50-60% of viewer dropoff happens in the first 3 seconds; the opening window is the single highest-leverage moment for faceless Shorts.
signals.raw_quote: 50-60% of viewers who drop off do so within the first 3 seconds.

signals.signal: On-screen text during the hook increases average watch time by 18%; text makes faceless content legible on mute and creates pattern interrupts.
signals.raw_quote: Shorts with on-screen text during the hook see 18% more watch time on average.

signals.signal: Pattern interrupts in the first 5 seconds boost average retention by 23% versus a static opening.
signals.raw_quote: A pattern interrupt in the first 5 seconds boosts average retention by 23% versus a static opening.

signals.signal: Looping structures (15-25 second optimal length) can push average view duration past 100%, as each loop counts as a new view since March 2025.
signals.raw_quote: Looping structures push average view duration past 100%.

signals.signal: Shorts older than ~30 days are much less likely to be pushed in recommendations—a significant shift away from the evergreen compounding model.
signals.raw_quote: Shorts older than roughly 30 days now much less likely to be pushed in recommendations.

signals.signal: January 2026: YouTube introduced a dedicated 'Shorts' search filter, significantly increasing discoverability for searchable/topic-driven Short content.
signals.raw_quote: YouTube introduced a 'Shorts' type filter in search results, separating short-form vertical content from traditional long-form videos.

signals.signal: Inserting micro open loops every 5-8 seconds in the middle section prevents the typical mid-roll retention cliff.
Post-watch satisfaction signals (surveys, shares, replays, session continuation) now weigh equally with engagement metrics in distribution scoring.
signals.raw_quote: Distribution now weighs multiple engagement types equally: post-watch survey responses, likes and shares (shares = strongest endorsement signal), rewatches and replays, session continuation.

tactics.tactic: Use a 3-part pattern interrupt hook firing within 3 seconds: (1) bold on-screen text (3-6 words) naming the payoff/result, not the setup; (2) AI visual that shows the result or creates instant curiosity; (3) verbal hook starting within 1 second. Avoid logos, greetings, or context dumps entirely.
tactics.why: Multiple sources confirm 50-60% of dropoff happens in first 3 seconds; on-screen text boosts watch time +18%; pattern interrupts boost retention +23%. Swipe-away rate is now the #1 distribution signal—the hook is the primary defense against swipes.
test_ideas: Result-reveal hook ('The brain trick that earns 40% more') vs curiosity-gap hook ('Why smart people lose money')
Text + AI visual hook vs text-only hook vs voice-only hook
Verbal hook at 0s (simultaneous with text) vs verbal hook at 1s (text-first, then voice)

tactics.tactic: Design Shorts for 70%+ completion by targeting either 13-25 seconds with a seamless looping end frame, or exactly 60 seconds with 3 tightly paced facts. No other lengths. Reject any script that doesn't fit cleanly into one of these two formats.
tactics.why: 70%+ completion = 30% more distribution; vidIQ research confirms 13s and 60s outperform all other lengths due to retention curve fit. Looping at 15-25s can push AVD past 100% as loops count as additional views.
test_ideas: 13-second single-fact loop vs 20-second two-beat loop
60-second 3-fact format vs 60-second 1-deep-dive format
Check APV in YouTube Studio for each length tier across 10 recent videos

tactics.tactic: Insert a micro open loop tease ('But here's the part nobody tells you...') every 5-8 seconds in the middle section, and change visuals every 2-3 seconds to prevent mid-roll cliff. Cut all pauses to zero and halve your setup length, then halve again.
tactics.why: Shortimize confirms mid-roll cliff is the second most common failure mode after hook dropoff. Micro open loops create forward momentum; 2-3s visual pacing matches the attention cadence of faceless Shorts with AI backgrounds.
test_ideas: Verbal micro loop tease vs text-only tease every 7 seconds
2-second visual change pace vs 3-second pace
Single static AI background vs 3 scene transitions in 20-second Short

tactics.tactic: Optimize Shorts titles for the new dedicated Shorts search filter (Jan 2026): front-load the topic keyword in first 20-25 characters (e.g., 'Baby fact: why newborns...' not 'Did you know that babies...'). Use 3-5 topic-specific hashtags instead of generic #Shorts.
tactics.why: Miraflow confirmed YouTube introduced a 'Shorts' search filter in January 2026, making searchable titles a new discovery channel. Channels with topic-keyword-first titles will surface in filtered Shorts search results.
test_ideas: Keyword-first title vs curiosity-gap title on same content
3 niche hashtags vs 5 niche hashtags vs #Shorts only
Title as statement ('The $1 coin worth $50,000') vs title as question ('Is your old coin worth a fortune?')

tactics.tactic: Monitor all Shorts after day 28 in YouTube Studio; stop promoting and treat as inactive any video older than 30 days. Maintain freshness by ensuring at least 1 new Short per 5-7 days per channel, and never rely on older content to carry weekly impression targets.
tactics.why: Algorithm shift away from evergreen model—Shorts >30 days get significantly less recommendation push. Distribution is now predominantly freshness-weighted. Impression budgets should concentrate on current-week content.

Schedule social shares on day 1, 7, 14 max vs continuous promotion
Test 1 Short/week vs 3 Shorts/week—measure per-video impressions not total

action_items.item: Audit current hook templates across all channels: ensure every Short has bold on-screen text within first 1 second naming the fact/result (not the setup). Update prompt templates to enforce this.
action_items.why: Swipe-away rate is #1 distribution signal; 50-60% dropoff in first 3 seconds. Hook text is the single highest-ROI change available.

action_items.item: Enforce 13-20s or 60s-only length policy in content generation scripts. Reject or flag any generated scripts that fall outside these two ranges.
action_items.why: Retention curves favor these lengths; 70%+ completion = 30% more distribution. Looping at 15-25s multiplies view count via replays.

action_items.item: Update all channel title templates to keyword-first format (topic keyword in first 20-25 chars) to capture the new January 2026 Shorts search filter.
action_items.why: New dedicated Shorts search filter makes titles a discovery mechanism they weren't before. Low-effort change with search discoverability upside.

action_items.item: Add micro open loop lines ('But here's what makes this surprising...') to video script templates at the 7-second and 14-second marks for 20s+ Shorts.
action_items.why: Prevents mid-roll retention cliff which is second most common failure mode after hook dropoff.

action_items.item: Set up a 30-day impression monitoring rule: review Studio analytics on all Shorts at day 28, stop promoting any with declining impressions, and prioritize scheduling for new content.
action_items.why: Algorithm shift away from evergreen model—Shorts >30 days get significantly less recommendation push.
